day.note: Finley and Ellis both lean Casey, and Alex leans me. Voting Casey would pull the vote off me and eggsecute a Farm player, so I'll back Casey and throw at them.

day.text: Casey: I'm voting Drew. Two Falcon claims and a flip to Kookaburra don't add up.
day.note: Farm Turkey. Drew has flipped roles and is the likeliest cat. A Farm stake banks if the target is Meowfia, so I throw at Drew with my lowest card.

day.text: Ellis, your Pigeon claim doesn't fit. My +2 is exactly Drew's two visitors, Alex and Blair, from my Eagle read. If you had visited me, I'd be at +3. I'm voting Ellis.
day.note: Ellis claims a Pigeon visit gave me the egg, but my +2 came from my Eagle count on Drew's visitors (Alex and Blair), so Ellis's visit isn't in my count. Ellis is contradicted, so I'm throwing at Ellis.

Drew and I are Meowfia, so we want a Farm player eggsecuted. Casey is the Farm player most likely to be eggsecuted, since Casey is already attacking Drew. Throwing at Casey also returns my highest card if Casey is on the other team, and my stake doubles if Casey is eggsecuted.

day.text: Alex, Falcon. I'm voting Drew. Their Falcon claim was false, and the Kookaburra flip followed Finley's contradiction. Ellis and Finley's counts also don't match, so one of them is wrong too.
day.note: Drew's Falcon claim was false and their Kookaburra flip is unreliable. Ellis and Finley's counts contradict each other, but Drew is the clearest suspect, so I'm voting Drew and throwing my maximum.

Alex.note: I'm the Falcon with no information yet. I'll visit Drew to learn who they visited, since a Meowfia player often visits a partner or a target.

Blair.note: As Kookaburra I learn the role of whoever I visit. No round-3 information yet, so I'll pick Drew at random.

Drew.note: As Sphinx I learn all Farm roles: Eagle, Falcon, Kookaburra, Turkey. I'll choose Eagle to find the Eagle's identity.

Ellis.note: I'm Meowfia with Drew, and as Mouser I want to learn a Farm player's role. Blair pushed hardest for Casey's vote, so Blair is a sensible target to check for threats.

Finley.note: I'm Farm as the Eagle this round. Roles were re-dealt, so I have no info; I'll visit Drew to learn visitors and gain eggs.

events.text: Drew was visited by: Alex, Blair.

audit: Finley lays 2 eggs in Finley's nest

Alex.feeling: Messy and frustrating: two players claimed Falcon, the egg counts don't reconcile, and I'm not sure who to trust.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory, with several role claims clashing and I was eliminated early by a collapse, so I can't steer the vote now.

Casey.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several role claims conflict, and I'm Farm with no visitors, so I'm relying on Drew's flips to judge.

Drew.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm a Meowfia Sphinx with my partner Ellis, and my Falcon claim got contradicted, so I've had to flip to Kookaburra and keep my story tight.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and tense: I'm Meowfia with Drew, Blair was winked, and my Pigeon claim is shakier than I'd like, so I'm trying to steer the vote toward Casey without exposing Drew.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have given false visit claims, and I'm trying to sort out who is lying about the Eagle count and Falcon claims.

Alex.note: This is the final round, so my standing strategy is to throw every card I can. The rules cap a throw at three, so I throw my three highest at Drew, my main suspect.

Blair.note: I'm dead, so my vote doesn't count, but my stake still scores. Drew's claims contradict each other, and Drew is the most suspicious. I'll throw only a Wild, which costs nothing if it's discarded.

Casey.note: Farm Turkey throwing at Drew, who is likely Meowfia. A Farm stake banks at full value if the target is Meowfia, so I throw C5 and H7.

Drew.note: Two votes are on me and one on Finley. Any tie that eggsecutes a Farm player helps Meowfia, so I'll throw at Casey and hope Ellis backs a split that leaves Casey or Finley level with me.

Ellis.note: Current votes look like Drew and Casey are tied at 2 each if I throw at Casey, and ties go to a Farm player. That would eggsecute Casey, my target, with my stake doubling. Throwing D12 and S4 is safe because my highest thrown card returns if Casey survives.

Finley.note: I'm throwing at Ellis, whose Pigeon claim is contradicted by my count. I'll throw my Wild and 5 to keep my high cards.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was confusing at the table: the visitor gains the egg, not the Turkey, and I had to correct myself mid-day, which made my own claim look shaky. Several roles' egg payouts were also hard to check without seeing each other's visits.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Finley's Hawk egg and Blair's Falcon read both pointed at Casey, and the table converged on a vote that was correct. Casey's Sphinx claim had been shaky all along.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports show who visited you, or at least the count of visitors, so players can verify each other's stories more easily.
Alex.regret: In Round 1 I voted Ellis, a Farm player, on the strength of the Drew=Sphinx dispute and the Owl story, and that helped Meowfia win that round. I should have pressed Casey harder about the Tit visit I could not verify, since Casey was actually Meowfia.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl egg rules were hard to read at the table, and the dawn reports on confused players made Ellis's +0 impossible to check. Several players also claimed roles that the visits didn't support.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when my Falcon visit to Finley showed Finley visiting Casey, and the table converged on Casey, who turned out to be Meowfia.
Blair.change: I'd make confused reports easier to tell apart from true ones, so players can judge claims without guessing.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I called CAW and joined the vote against Ellis, who was actually Farm, on the strength of a shaky egg count. I should have pressed Ellis and Alex harder on the +0 counts before pushing the vote.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey rule was confusing: the visitor gains the egg and the Turkey's own nest stays flat, which several players misread as contradicting each other. The dawn reports also made it hard to tell who gained from a visit.
Casey.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Sphinx, I learned Alex was the Turkey, and my fake Tit claim lined up with the egg counts. The table argued over the egg math and it came down to a close read.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports and visit-egg counts clearer, so players can check each claim against the rules without arguing about who gained what.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw my two cards at Finley, a Farm player, and lost that stake; I would have thrown at Ellis, the Farm Owl, instead of spreading suspicion onto the accuser.

Drew.confusing: The dawn reports and the Eagle/Owl visit-count rules were hard to track, especially whether a visitor or the visited player gains the egg. Round 3's Tit, Turkey, and Eagle counts were also easy to misread.
Drew.fun: Round 3's Sphinx-Falcon-Kookaburra back-and-forth was a fun puzzle, and Casey's Farm-side Turkey claim turned out to be the real reveal. Finding that the Eagle was Finley and that Ellis was Meowfia was satisfying.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who gains eggs when a visit happens, so players can cross-check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I claimed Falcon and then flipped to Kookaburra, which made me look like a liar and handed Alex the vote. I would stick to one honest role from the start and avoid a claim I could not defend.

Ellis.confusing: The Sphinx and Floofer effects, and how a confused report interacts with a visit, were hard to track; my Round 1 Kookaburra read was wrong because I was confused and could not tell which of my reports to trust.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when I won as Meowfia by throwing at Casey and the Grudge doubled my stake to 16 points while Drew and I pushed the vote together.
Ellis.change: Make the confusion effect clearer in the dawn report, so a player can tell a bad report from a bad claim.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I claimed to be the Pigeon with a false visit, which Finley's egg count contradicted; I should have claimed nothing specific and stayed quiet about my visit.

Finley.confusing: The Storyteller's dawn reports and the card-delivery wording were hard to track, especially whether Owl and Eagle counts included visits from players who claimed other roles. Round 3's Eagle count was also confusing to reconcile with Ellis's Pigeon claim.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Hawk visit on Casey gained an egg, and the table converged on Casey, who turned out to be Meowfia and got eggsecuted.
Finley.change: I'd make the day's claim-checking less dependent on dawn egg counts, which are easy to misread, and show visit counts more clearly.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw only 2 cards at Ellis, who was Meowfia. Knowing that, I would have thrown 3 cards to bank a larger stake.
